sentences: A proper hypergraph coloring assigns colors to vertices so that no hyperedge is monochromatic.
The promise here is that every hyperedge has three vertices and that a two-coloring exists.
The question asks whether finding a coloring with more than a logarithm-of-logarithm number of colors is NP-hard, or at least quasi-NP-hard.
The source obtains stronger coloring hardness for four-uniform hypergraphs, where one additional vertex per edge gives reductions more flexibility.
Transferring comparable hardness to triples would sharpen the boundary of what efficient algorithms can do under a very strong colorability promise.
